sentences.text:
Cra No. 572 of 2005
  Ram Bharos, S/o.

Late Manbodh, Aged 24 years,
 Occupation : Agriculture, R/o Village Rampur, P.S. Ambikapur  (Rural) District-Sarguja (C.G.)
 ---- Appellant  Versus   State of Chhattisgarh, Through : District Magistrate, District -  Sarguja (C.G.)
 ---- Respondent For Appellant - Shri Atul K. Kesharwani, Advocate appears on behalf of Shri S.R.J. Jaiswal,
Advocate.
For State/Respondent - Shri Pawan Kesharwani, Panel Lawyer.
Hon'ble Shri Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal Order on Board 15.01.2024 1.

This appeal arise out of judgment of conviction and sentence dated 13.06.2005 passed by 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Ambikapur District - Surguja in Sessions Trial No.338/2004, whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offence under Section 450 of IPC and sentenced for R.I. for 7 years with fine of Rs.100/- in default of payment of fine further R.I. for 1 month and also for the offence under Section 376 of IPC and sentenced for R.I. for 7 years with fine of Rs.100/- in default of payment of fine further R.I. for 1 month.

entities.text: 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Ambikapur District - Surguja
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The sentences are directed to run concurrently.

2. Brief facts of the case are that on 11.05.2004, the prosecutrix (PW-9) aged about 20 years has lodged a report to the Police Station - Gandhi Nagar District - Surguja against the appellant alleging him that she is having dispute with her husband and therefore she is residing at her parent's house since one and half year back.

entities.text: Police Station - Gandhi Nagar District - Surguja
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Yesterday, she was at her home at about 04:00 PM when she came back from the well, the appellant came there and caught hold her, when she tried to save herself and shouted, her brother Anu and mother came there, her brother had make a noise pksj & pksj and thereafter number of persons have gathered there and thereafter she informed the incident to her parent and lodged the report.

3. On the report of prosecutrix (PW-9) the police has registered the offence under Section 354 of IPC vide Ex.P/5, after 3 days of lodging of the report by the prosecutrix for commission of offence of outraging modesty, she has made complaint against the appellant that on 10.05.2004 she was subjected to rape by the appellant thereafter the police has started investigation considering to be Rambharos vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28589463/
1 the offence of Section 376 of IPC.

The prosecutrix was sent for her medical examination to Government Hospital, Ambikapur, where Dr. Smt. Lata Goyal (PW-11) has examined her and gave her report Ex.P/10, whereby she has opined that the prosecutrix is habitual for sexual intercourse,
no definite opinion can be given regarding recent intercourse.
Two slides of vaginal smear have been prepared, sealed and handed over for chemical analysis.
While examining the prosecutrix the doctor has not noticed any injury over her body.
The spot map Ex.P/8 was prepared by the police.
The appellant was also arrested on 12.05.2004 under the offence of Section 354 of IPC and the police has released him on his bail bond.

Subsequently, when the allegation of rape was made by the prosecutrix against him, he was again taken into custody on 18.05.2004 and he too was sent for his medical examination to the Government Hospital, Ambikapur where he has been medically examined by Dr. Azad Bhagat (PW-7) who gave the report Ex.P/5 and opined that he is capable to perform sexual intercourse.
The undergarment of the appellant was seized.

The glass slides prepared from the vaginal smear of the prosecutrix and the under garment of the appellant were sent for FSL examination from where the FSL report Ex.P/16 was received and in the vaginal smear and the under garment of the appellant, no semen or sperms were found.
After recording statements of witnesses under Section 161 of CrPC the police have filed charge-sheet against the appellant for the offence under Section 354, 376 & 450 of IPC.
4. After committal of the case for trial, the trial Court has framed charges under Section 450 & 376 of IPC against the appellant.
The appellant absurd his guilt and claimed trial.
5. In order to establish the charge against the appellant the prosecution has examined 13 witnesses.

The statement under Section 313 of CrPC of the appellant was also recorded in which he denied the material appears against him and submitted that he has lodged the report against Ramu, Ramlal and Suritram, he has not entered into the house of the prosecutrix and has not committed any offence.
There was no any Panchayat meeting convened.
All the above three persons have detained him.
He went there for answering the call of nature.
A fine of Rs.3,000/- has not been imposed upon him by the panchayat and he has been falsely implicated in the offence.
After appreciation of the evidence available on record the trial Court has convicted the appellant and sentenced him as mentioned in para-1 of this judgment.
Hence, this appeal.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant would argue that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the offence.
Prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.

Initially the prosecutrix has lodged the report for committing the offence of outraging her modesty, subsequently she improved in her stand and allegation of rape has been levelled by her which itself shows that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the offence.
Had she been subjected to rape by the appellant she would have lodged the report regarding rape on very first instance.
There are material omission and contradictions in evidences of prosecution witnesses and therefore the appellant is entitled for the benefit of doubt.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that appellant is the person who has been assaulted by the 3 villagers and detained in the courtyard of the prosecutrix for which he has lodged report to the police against the 3 persons and in order to save themselves they made the prosecutrix instrumental and have lodged the report against him.

The lodging of report by the accused at earlier point of time is admitted by the witnesses as well as the father of the prosecutrix,
who have specifically stated in his deposition that

since the accused has already lodged the report Rambharos vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28589463/
2 against them and therefore in order to save themselves he has lodged the present report.

He would further argued that the prosecutrix herself stated that she could not identified the accused therefore in view of the totality of the evidence, the appellant is entitled atleast for benefit of doubt and is entitled for acquittal.
7.

On the other hand learned counsel for the State/respondent would vehemently opposes the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant and submitted that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.
The evidence of the prosecutrix as well as her family member are reliable.
But for minor contradiction their evidences are corroborative.
The appellant was caught red-handed inside the house of the prosecutrix.
Lodging the report against 3 other persons, it would not have any effect in this case.
Therefore, the learned trial Court has rightly convicted the appellant and impugned judgment of conviction and sentence needs no interference.
8. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9. The PW-9 the prosecutrix have stated in para-1 of her deposition that she has not identified the accused and she has not seen him ever before.
She was again asked but she remained firm that she has not identified the accused.
She has further stated in her deposition that when she has returned from the well the appellant came there and committed rape upon her.
When she was shouted, he gagged her mouth by gamcha and when she was thrown on the ground and pressed her breast she came out by weeping.
Except pressing her breast he did not do anything else.
At that time her brother shouted and so many persons were gathered who have caught hold the appellant and in the next morning she went to lodge the report alongwith her father and villagers.
The police has recorded her statements only once and not twice.
10. In cross examination she has stated that though she is married, she is residing with her parents.
In the police station she has stated that the appellant has pressed her breast and admitted the lodging of report Ex.P/5.
The police persons were shown their angerness and said that don't come to lodge the report on the instance of Juglal, Ranglal and Manbahal.
Police has not recorded her second statement.
She denied giving her second statement Ex.D/7.
In para - 16 of her cross examination, she again reiterated that the person who caught hold her hand she could not identify him.
Again she has stated that the person who had committed rape upon her, she could not identified him.
In para-17 of her cross examination she again stated that the incident of rape she has stated first time today.
In para-18 she again voluntarily stated that she had never seen him earlier.

11. PW-2, mother of the prosecutrix have stated in her deposition that when she returned to her house after ploughing the vegetables the door of her house was open and no one is there in the house when she call her daughter her daughter came out from inside the house in very hasty manner, thereafter his son entered into the house and informed that someone has entered into the house then the villagers gathered there and her daughter went out from back side of her house,
when she asked from her daughter she only disclosed that someone has entered into the house except this no any other incident she disclosed.
Her daughter has only informed her that the appellant has only caught hold her.
She has stated that her son had gone alongwith her.
In para-7 she has stated that the appellant was detained in her courtyard by the villagers.

She further stated Rambharos vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28589463/
3 that her daughter has not disclosed the incident to her that the appellant has caught hold her hand and breast.

She admits that Suritram is the son of her brother in law (son of husband's younger brother).
12. PW-3, who is father of the prosecutrix have stated in his deposition that at the time of incident he was in brother's house where his son Anu came and called him and informed him that someone has entered inside their house.
When he came back to his house her daughter informed about the incident and at that time the villagers have detained the accused and thereafter they went to lodged the report to the police.
He has deposed up to after 3-4 days of the incident her daughter has not disclosed any incident to him.
In cross examination he has stated that the villagers have narrate him that they have beaten the accused.
He admits in para-8 that on the next day he came to know that the appellant/accused has lodged report against Ramu, Ramlal and Suritram against the alleged assault made with him.
In para-9 this witness has specifically admitted after coming into knowledge about the fact that the appellant has lodged the report against them.
In order to save themselves they have lodged the report against the appellant.
He further admits that in the police station the prosecutrix has lodged the report regarding outraging of her modesty.
It is further admitted by him that initially they have lodged the report for outraging the modesty and subsequently lodged the report regarding rape.
In para-13 he again admitted that since the appellant has lodged the report against them they also have lodged report against the appellant.
If the appellant would have done the polite behaviour with them, they would not have done anything against him.
13. PW-5, who is the brother of the prosecutrix have stated that he does not know the accused and never seen him before.
When he returned back from the Badi, he saw that the appellant is there inside his house, he raised the noise and the villagers gathered there and thereafter he called his father.
In cross examination he has stated that during the police statement he has not stated before the police that the appellant was committing rape upon her.
He further admitted that he has not seen the incident and it is Juglal who entered his house and he has not entered inside the house.
Neither he asked from his sister nor she has disclosed anything to him about the incident.
14. PW-6, neighbour of the prosecutrix who has stated that on the date of incident after hearing the noise he went on the spot and at that time so many persons were gathered.
They taken out the accused from the house and at that time prosecutrix informed them that the accused was following her and entered inside the house and has committed rape upon her.
In para-6 of his cross examination he has admitted that the Chowkidar has tied the hands of the accused and was detained in the courtyard of the prosecutrix.

He admitted that due to the illicit relationship by the prosecutrix with some other person, her in- laws have left her and thereafter she is residing in her parents'
house.
He admitted that when they went to the police station, the police persons have informed them that the accused has lodged the report against 3 persons.
He further admits that on 14.05.2002 the prosecutrix has disclosed the incident of rape and on 10th she has not disclosed any incident of rape.
15. The doctor who has medically examined the prosecutrix has not noticed any injuries over her body either external or internal.
No any siemens or sperms are found in the vaginal smear of the prosecutrix.

The appellant has produced the document Ex.D/2 which is his defence that the 3 Rambharos vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28589463/
4 persons namely Ramu, Ramlal and Suritram has assaulted him when he went to the house of the prosecutrix and asked for water and they have beaten and taken him inside the house of the prosecutrix and detained there.

The lodging of the report at earlier point in the time was admitted by the father of the prosecutrix PW/3 and said that since the accused has lodged the report against them and therefore in order to save themselves they have also lodged the report against the accused.

The PW/2 has stated that Suritram is the son of her brother in law (son of husband's younger brother) so the father of the prosecutrix is interested in the report lodged by the accused against Ramu, Ramlal and Suritram and therefore possibility of false implication to save themselves from the report lodged by the accused cannot be ruled out.
Had she been subjected to forceful sexual intercourse by the accused, she would have immediately lodged the report for the offence of commission of rape.
There is no reason to conceal that part of the offence and to lodged the report only for commission of offence of outraging her modesty.
From the evidences of the witnesses it appears that the accused was detained in the courtyard of the prosecutrix by tiding her hand and so many persons of the village were gathered.

16. Considering the entire evidence available on record, facts and circumstances of the case particularly considering the FIR lodged by the accused Ex.D/2 and also the admissions made by the witnesses changing stand of prosecutrix from outraging modesty to the allegation of rape, the accused is entitled for benefit of doubt and therefore, the offence against him has not been found proved beyond reasonable doubt.
17. In the result the appeal is allowed.
18. The appellant is acquitted from the charges under Section 450, 376 of IPC.

He is on bail, his bail bond shall continue for further period of six month as provided under Section 437A of CrPC.
19.
The lower court records along with a copy of this judgment be sent back immediately to the trial court, concerned for compliance and necessary action.

Sd/-
